kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the two printed tables — 4 patterns (scombroid's anaphylaxis mimic, tetrodotoxin's silenced nerve, ciguatoxin's hot/cold reversal, the mad-honey-vs-jimsonweed autonomic fork), 4 traps (scombroid vs true IgE fish allergy, tetrodotoxin-block vs ciguatoxin-open, grayanotoxin vs cardiac glycosides, coniine-nicotinic vs atropine/scopolamine-muscarinic), 3 pivots, 8 recall cards — with the treatment column additionally dissected in the exam callout and the drug cards.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid supplies the tables' facts only; the attack structure, the distractor designs, and the target-routing discipline are KYP's design.

kypExtensions.summary: The three-move reading protocol (NAME THE TARGET → PREDICT THE SYMPTOMS FROM THE TARGET'S PHYSIOLOGY → LET THE ANTIDOTE FOLLOW THE TARGET), including the Na+ channel fork framing (total block vs opening) and the observation that the molecular target — never the fish or plant name — is the answer key for mechanism, symptom, and treatment questions alike.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints two parallel tables and never asks the learner to route a stem through target → physiology → antidote; the protocol and the fork framing are KYP's synthesis.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea + blocks[4] the steps block + the registry visual's fork band

kypExtensions.summary: The four KYP mnemonics (PUFFER BLOCKS, REEF OPENS, SPOILED POURS / MAD HONEY, MAD VAGUS / SITE 2 SUSTAINS THE STORM / NICOTINIC PARALYZES, MUSCARINIC DRIES). No mnemonic prints in the page's margins; First Aid's own RED mnemonic furniture — the intro sentence's initial letters h/t/c and the red first letters H/T/C on the seafood toxin names — is carried ATTRIBUTED inside the note and is NOT counted among the four KYP codes.
kypExtensions.rationale: No margin mnemonic prints anywhere on pdf 268 (pdfimages + VLM census, staging-ph21/vlm-census.txt); the four ALL-CAPS codes are KYP's design.
kypExtensions.location: mnemonics + blocks[6] the memory callout + the visual's panel footers

kypExtensions.summary: The five DrugCards for the printed treatment agents (physostigmine, atropine-as-antidote, digoxin-specific Fab, activated charcoal, antihistamines + albuterol +/– epinephrine) — one card per antidote lane, each traced to the TREATMENT cell that prints it. Convention, documented: the page prints no adverse-effects column for these agents, so each card's adverse field is explicitly labeled 'Not printed on book 246' and states the general pharmacology (e.g., physostigmine's cholinergic excess, Fab's hypokalemia) rather than implying a printed source.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source organizes treatments as table cells, not as drug cards; the card layer is a KYP presentation — every mechanism/uses string quotes the printed treatment cell, and the adverse fields are flagged as outside the print.

kypExtensions.summary: The MAOI–scombroid interaction note: patients on MAO inhibitors can have exaggerated scombroid reactions because ingested amines are normally cleared by oxidative deamination. This is a KYP extension that does NOT print on book 246 — it is carried in exactly three clearly-labeled places (one trap's clue, one crossLink, and the visual's warning band, each labeled 'KYP extension (not printed on book 246)') and is never presented as printed content.
kypExtensions.rationale: The batch content map expected the scombroid–MAOI interaction on this page, but no MAOI text prints on pdf 268 (VLM-confirmed); the interaction is real toxicology teaching, so it is carried as clearly-labeled KYP extension knowledge rather than fabricated print.
